mainTopic: What counts as שגגה for a חטאת: מונבז vs. רבנן, רבי יוחנן vs. ריש לקיש, the 39 מלאכות, and אביי on שבועת ביטוי
overview: This amud opens with the רבנן's source that a חטאת is brought only for a sin whose deliberate version carries כרת. The source is a היקש comparing the whole Torah to עבודה זרה. מונבז holds that a person counts as a שוגג even if he only did not know about the קרבן, but the רבנן reject this. Among the רבנן, רבי יוחנן says not knowing about the כרת is enough, while ריש לקיש requires not knowing about both the לאו and the כרת. רבי יוחנן uses ריש לקיש's פסוק for a different law: a משומד does not bring a חטאת. The גמרא then tests ריש לקיש with the משנה of the 39 מלאכות, where a person knew about שבת but not the מלאכות. It answers that he knew about תחומין, which is a Torah law according to רבי עקיבא. A ברייתא that counts someone as a שוגג when he did not know only about the קרבן is shown to follow מונבז. Finally, אביי teaches that for a שבועת ביטוי, a קרבן is brought only if the person did not know the לאו, and the גמרא explains why this needed to be said.

steps.title: The whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים about עבודה זרה show that a חטאת applies only to sins whose deliberate violation brings כרת. The whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says: 'And if you err and do not do all these commandments.' It also says: 'And the person who acts with a high hand' (that soul will be cut off). All the מצוות are compared to עבודה זרה. With עבודה זרה, the sin brings כרת if done on purpose and a חטאת if done by mistake. So too, any sin that brings כרת on purpose brings a חטאת by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes giving the source for why a חטאת is brought only for sins that carry כרת when done on purpose. It does this by comparing all sins to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק is about mistaken עבודה זרה, which requires a חטאת. The second פסוק, 'ביד רמה', gives כרת for the deliberate sinner. Because the Torah links all the מצוות to עבודה זרה, the same pattern applies everywhere: a sin brings a חטאת only if its deliberate version carries כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared (a הֶקֵּשׁ, a comparison drawn from how the verses are placed together)
With a high hand, meaning boldly and on purpose
Sin-offering brought for a mistaken sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש is the basis for the general rule that a חטאת is brought only for a sin whose deliberate version carries כרת.

phrases.english: "And if you err and do not perform
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:22. This פסוק is read as talking about עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: all these commandments",
and it is written: "And the person who acts with a high hand"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:30. That פסוק goes on to give כרת.

phrases.english: All of them are compared to idolatry:
Just as there, it is a matter
for whose deliberate violation one is liable to karet
and for its unwitting violation, a sin-offering,
so too, any matter
for whose deliberate violation one is liable to karet
and for its unwitting violation, a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבנן's source derivation from the previous part of the daf
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a חטאת applies only to sins carrying כרת when done on purpose
steps.raayaSupportSource: Numbers 15:22 and 15:30, read as a היקש of the whole Torah to עבודה זרה

steps.title: How does מונבז define an unwitting sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of mistake מונבז has in mind. In his view, someone who knew the act was forbidden can still count as a שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to מונבז, what was the person mistaken about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking a clarifying question. If מונבז says a person who knew about the prohibition is still a שוגג, what was that person unaware of?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מונבז holds that even someone aware that the act was forbidden can bring a חטאת. That sounds strange, since a person who knew seems to be sinning on purpose. So the גמרא asks what exactly the 'mistake' was.

keyTerms.meaning: מונבז, a king who held a broad definition of an unwitting sin
In what way was it unwitting?

phrases.english: But according to Munbaz, in what way was it unwitting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the source of the rule to the definition of שגגה in מונבז's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of lack of knowledge makes a person a שוגג according to מונבז

steps.title: He was unaware of the sacrifice obligation
steps.stepSummary: For מונבז, it is enough that the person did not know a חטאת is required for this sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, when he was mistaken about the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about מונבז. The person knew the act was forbidden and even carried כרת, but he did not know it required a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מונבז holds that missing any part of the law's consequences, even just the קרבן, makes the sin a שגגה. So a person who knew about the prohibition but not the חטאת still brings one.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where
He was mistaken regarding the sacrifice

steps.confusionAlert: Do not misread this as 'he made a mistake while bringing a קרבן.' It means he did not know that this sin obligates a קרבן.

phrases.english: For example, where he was unwitting regarding the sacrifice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For מונבז, not knowing about the קרבן obligation is enough to count as שגגה

steps.title: The רבנן reject unawareness of the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that not knowing about the קרבן does not make a sin a שגגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: being mistaken only about the קרבן is not called being mistaken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן disagree with מונבז. For them, not knowing about the קרבן alone does not count as a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, a true שגגה must involve not knowing something about the sin itself, not just about the atonement process. This raises the obvious next question: what must a person be unaware of, according to the רבנן?

keyTerms.meaning: Is not called an unwitting act

phrases.english: And the Rabbis:
unwittingness regarding a sacrifice is not considered unwittingness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's opposing view to מונבז's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not knowing about the קרבן alone does not make a sin a שגגה

steps.title: How do the רבנן define an unwitting sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lack of knowledge does count as a mistake for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, what was the person mistaken about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next debate. It asks what a person must be unaware of to count as a שוגג in the רבנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that not knowing about the קרבן has been ruled out, we need to know the minimum the person must not know. The answer will be a מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, in what way is it unwitting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the רבנן's rejection of מונבז
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum lack of knowledge that counts as שגגה for the רבנן

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: unaware of כרת is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that if the person did not know about the כרת, it is a שגגה, even if he knew there was a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: as long as he was mistaken about the כרת, even though he did the לאו on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer. Not knowing that the sin carries כרת is enough to make it a שגגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, knowing that the act is forbidden by a לאו does not make the sin deliberate. What matters is not knowing the severe consequence, כרת, since כרת is what makes a sin fit for a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יוחנן, a leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Since he was unwitting regarding karet,
even though he was deliberate regarding the prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁשָּׁגַג בְּכָרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not knowing about the כרת alone is enough for שגגה

steps.title: ריש לקיש: must be unaware of both
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says it is a שגגה only if the person knew neither the לאו nor the כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: not until he is mistaken about both the לאו and the כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a stricter, competing answer. The person must not know that the act is forbidden at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, if the person knew there was a לאו, he is treated as acting on purpose, even if he did not know about the כרת. Only total lack of knowledge of the prohibition counts as a שגגה.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש (רבי שמעון בן לקיש), רבי יוחנן's colleague

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Not until he is unwitting regarding both the prohibition and karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁגּוֹג בְּלָאו וְכָרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן's answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person must not know about either the לאו or the כרת

steps.title: רבא gives ריש לקיש's verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ריש לקיש learns from the פסוק 'אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם' that the person must not know about the לאו and its כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is ריש לקיש's reason? The פסוק says: 'which may not be done, by mistake, and he becomes guilty.' This means he must be mistaken about the לאו and the כרת that goes with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא provides the scriptural source for ריש לקיש's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשר לא תעשינה' ('which may not be done') describe the prohibition itself, the לאו. Since the פסוק puts these words right next to 'בשגגה', ריש לקיש reads it to mean the mistake must include not knowing the לאו, not just the כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Which may not be done, referring to a prohibition

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ —
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish?
The verse said:
"That may not be done, unwittingly, and he becomes guilty"
not until he is unwitting regarding the prohibition and its karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for ריש לקיש's view in step 7
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's requirement of not knowing about both the לאו and the כרת

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן do with this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק that ריש לקיש relies on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what does he do with this פסוק of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by challenging רבי יוחנן. If the פסוק seems to require not knowing the לאו, why doesn't he accept that reading, and what does he learn from it instead?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is not supposed to be extra. If רבי יוחנן does not read it the way ריש לקיש does, he needs another use for it. Otherwise ריש לקיש's proof would stand against him.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (how does he use the verse)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: this verse of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns ריש לקיש's proof into a question against רבי יוחנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוחנן learns from 'אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם'
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that not knowing about the כרת alone is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק appears to require not knowing the לאו, so רבי יוחנן must account for it

steps.title: רבי יוחנן uses it for a ברייתא about a משומד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן needs the פסוק for a ברייתא about excluding a משומד. The first opinion there learns this from 'מעם הארץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'From the common people' excludes a משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק for a different law, found in a ברייתא. It begins quoting that ברייתא: the first opinion learns from 'מעם הארץ' that a משומד does not bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that a משומד does not bring a חטאת for a mistaken sin. According to the first opinion, the source is 'מעם הארץ'. The next opinion in the ברייתא will use ריש לקיש's very words for this law, and that is the opinion רבי יוחנן follows.

keyTerms.meaning: For that which was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught in a baraita:
"From the common people": this excludes an apostate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק must teach that a person has to be unaware of the לאו
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that a משומד does not bring a חטאת

steps.title: Only one who would repent brings a sacrifice
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבי שמעון, learns from 'אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם' that only a person who would turn back once he found out brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי שמעון: 'which may not be done, by mistake, and he becomes guilty.' One who would turn back from the sin once he learns of it brings a קרבן for his mistake. One who would not turn back once he learns of it does not bring a קרבן for his mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in the ברייתא. It learns the exclusion of a משומד from the same פסוק ריש לקיש used. רבי יוחנן follows this opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a person who sinned by mistake and would have held back had he known it was forbidden. A person who would keep sinning even after learning the truth is not a real שוגג. Since רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק for this law, it is not available to prove ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a תנא
One who turns back once he becomes aware

steps.whatToRemember: מונבז: not knowing about the קרבן alone counts as a mistake. רבנן: it does not. Among the רבנן, רבי יוחנן says not knowing about the כרת is enough. ריש לקיש requires not knowing about both the לאו and the כרת. רבי יוחנן uses ריש לקיש's פסוק to exclude a משומד, who would not turn back once he knew.
steps.whyThisMatters: A חטאת is not just a penalty. It fits only a person who would have avoided the sin had he known.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
"That may not be done, unwittingly, and he becomes guilty."
One who would turn back upon his awareness
brings a sacrifice for his unwitting sin;
one who would not turn back upon his awareness
does not bring a sacrifice for his unwitting sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and shows the exact use רבי יוחנן makes of ריש לקיש's פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone who would turn back once he knew brings a חטאת, so a משומד is excluded, learned from 'אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם'

steps.title: Bringing in the counting of the 39 מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that there are 39 main מלאכות, along with רבי יוחנן's explanation of why the number is given. That explanation describes a case of זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: the main categories of work are forty minus one. We asked about this: why do I need the number? רבי יוחנן said: to teach that if someone did all of them during one period of forgetting, he is liable for each one. How can you find such a case? When he knew it was שבת but did not know these acts were forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing in a source it will use to test ריש לקיש's opinion. This step is a setup, and the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the number 39 teaches that a person can bring 39 separate חטאות. That only works if he 'knew it was שבת' but did not know the מלאכות were forbidden. The question will be what exactly he knew about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The main categories of forbidden work on שבת
Knowing that it is שבת and that שבת has prohibitions
Not knowing that these specific acts are forbidden

phrases.english: We learned in a Mishnah: the primary categories of labor
are forty less one.
And we discussed it: why do I need the number?
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness
he is liable for each and every one.
How can you find this case?
When he knew about Shabbat but was unaware about the labors.
phrases.notes: This is the key phrase the next step will press on.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test ריש לקיש's definition of שגגה from Step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person can be liable for all 39 מלאכות in one העלם in a case of זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות

steps.title: What did he know about שבת according to ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוחנן, 'knowing שבת' easily means knowing the לאו but not the כרת. For ריש לקיש, who requires not knowing the לאו at all, it is unclear what the person knew.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יוחנן, who says that once he did not know about the כרת he is שוגג, even if he knew about the לאו. You can find the case where he knew שבת has a לאו. But for ריש לקיש, who says he must not know both the לאו and the כרת, what did he know about שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש. If the person must not know the לאו of the מלאכות, what part of שבת did he know about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, 'זדון שבת' simply means he knew there is a לאו, and 'שגגת מלאכות' means he did not know about the כרת. For ריש לקיש the person did not even know the לאו of every מלאכה. So it seems there is nothing left for him to have 'known' about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for, which introduces a contrast
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for intentional חילול שבת

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yochanan,
who said: once he was unwitting about karet,
even though he was intentional regarding the prohibition,
you can find it, for example,
where he knew Shabbat in terms of its prohibition.
But according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
who said: not until he is unwitting about both the prohibition and karet,
in what way did he know Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the case from Step 12 to both opinions and finds a difficulty for ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that שגגה requires not knowing both לאו and כרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he did not know the לאו of any מלאכה, nothing remains for 'זדון שבת' to mean

steps.title: He knew about תחומין
steps.stepSummary: The person knew the Torah law of תחומין, following רבי עקיבא, who holds that תחומין is a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He knew about the boundaries (תחומין), according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש. The person knew that שבת has the Torah prohibition of תחומין, even though he did not know about the 39 מלאכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זדון שבת' does not have to mean knowing about the מלאכות. It can mean knowing a different Torah law of שבת. רבי עקיבא holds that תחומין is a דאורייתא, so knowing it counts as knowing שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The limit on how far one may walk outside the city on שבת
The תנא who holds that תחומין is a Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, 'זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות' means he knew about תחומין (a Torah law according to רבי עקיבא) but did not know about the מלאכות at all.

phrases.english: He knew it in terms of Shabbat boundaries,
and according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: 'knowing שבת' refers to a different Torah law of שבת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Knowing שבת must mean knowing the לאו of the מלאכות
steps.terutzMaskana: It can mean knowing the Torah law of תחומין, following רבי עקיבא

steps.title: Who taught this ברייתא about kinds of שוגג?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא listing cases of שוגג. Its last case makes a person liable even when he knew the act was forbidden and only did not know about the קרבן. The גמרא asks whose opinion this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the רבנן taught? If he was unaware of both, that is the שוגג the Torah speaks about. If he knew both, that is the מזיד the Torah speaks about. If he forgot it was שבת but knew the acts were forbidden, or did not know the acts were forbidden but knew it was שבת, or said 'I know this work is forbidden, but I don't know whether it brings a קרבן', he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks which תנא holds it. The last case is very lenient about what counts as שוגג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last case is the surprising one. The person knew the act was forbidden and knew there was a punishment. He only did not know there is a קרבן, and still he counts as שוגג. That goes even further than רבי יוחנן, who requires not knowing the כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא who taught this?

steps.confusionAlert: 'בזה ובזה' means שבת and the מלאכות. It does not mean the לאו and the כרת.

phrases.english: Who taught this,
that the Rabbis taught:
If he was unwitting in this and that,
that is the unwitting sinner stated in the Torah.
If he was intentional in this and that,
that is the intentional sinner stated in the Torah.
If he was unwitting about Shabbat and intentional about the labors,
or unwitting about the labors and intentional about Shabbat,
or if he said: I know
that this labor is forbidden,
but I do not know
whether one is liable a sacrifice for it or not,
he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related question about how little lack of knowledge is enough for שגגה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that not knowing about the קרבן alone is enough to be שוגג

steps.title: The ברייתא follows מונבז
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows מונבז, who holds that not knowing about the קרבן alone is enough to make someone שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom? Like מונבז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows מונבז, who holds this lenient view of שוגג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מונבז holds that not knowing about the קרבן is enough to bring a קרבן. The חכמים argue with him. So the ברייתא is not the view of רבי יוחנן or ריש לקיש, who both require more lack of knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: מונבז, a king whose opinion is quoted in ברייתות. He holds that not knowing about the קרבן alone is enough to be שוגג.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Munbaz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15

steps.title: אביי: for שבועת ביטוי a person must not know the לאו
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that everyone agrees a person brings a קרבן for breaking a שבועת ביטוי only if he did not know the לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees about a שבועת ביטוי that a person is liable a קרבן only if he did not know its לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new rule about a שבועת ביטוי. Not knowing about the קרבן is not enough here. The person must not know the לאו itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבועת ביטוי has a לאו but no כרת. So the person's lack of knowledge has to be about the לאו. The words 'everyone agrees' suggest that someone who is usually lenient agrees here, and the גמרא will ask who that is.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath someone makes about himself, such as 'I will eat' or 'I won't eat'
An אמורא who gives this rule

phrases.english: Abaye said: Everyone agrees
regarding an oath on a statement,
that one is not liable a sacrifice for it
unless he is unwitting about its prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּשְׁבוּעַת בִּיטּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement about the level of שגגה needed when there is no כרת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For שבועת ביטוי, a קרבן is brought only if the person did not know the לאו

steps.title: 'Everyone agrees' refers to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who 'everyone' includes, meaning who might have disagreed, and answers רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone agrees': who is meant? רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who אביי meant to include in 'everyone', and answers that it is רבי יוחנן. This answer sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן usually says a person is שוגג even if he knew the לאו, as long as he did not know the כרת. So אביי seems to be saying that even רבי יוחנן agrees about שבועת ביטוי.

phrases.english: 'Everyone agrees': who is meant?
Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording of אביי's statement in Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Everyone' is meant to include רבי יוחנן

steps.title: That is obvious: רבי יוחנן only spoke about כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי needed to say this. רבי יוחנן's leniency only applies where there is כרת, and שבועת ביטוי has no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! When רבי יוחנן spoke, it was where there is כרת. But here, where there is no כרת, he would not say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's statement as obvious. Of course רבי יוחנן agrees when there is no כרת. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule is 'he did not know the כרת, even though he knew the לאו'. Where there is no כרת at all, the only thing a person can fail to know is the לאו. So it seems אביי taught nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: That is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: That is obvious!
When Rabbi Yochanan said his rule,
it was where there is karet;
but here, where there is no karet, he would not say so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification in Step 18 as making אביי's statement unnecessary
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement as explained in Step 18
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's leniency depends on there being a כרת, so with no כרת his agreement is obvious and there is no חידוש

steps.title: Without אביי, we might have treated the unusual oath law more broadly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why אביי's statement was needed. Since bringing a קרבן for שבועת ביטוי is already a חידוש, one might have thought that not knowing about the קרבן alone would be enough to make him liable. אביי teaches that this is not so.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought this: Bringing a קרבן here is a special rule. In the whole Torah we never find a לאו without כרת for which a person brings a קרבן, yet here he does bring one. So maybe even if he only did not know about the קרבן, he should also be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question 'why did אביי need to say this?' It shows what mistake we might have made without his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 argued that אביי's ruling was obvious. רבי יוחנן's leniency is tied to כרת, and שבועת ביטוי has no כרת. The answer is that שבועת ביטוי is already an exception to the normal pattern, so we might have guessed its rules are broader too. אביי closes that door: even here, he brings a קרבן only if he did not know the לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: It might enter your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken first thought (הוה אמינא).
A novel law that breaks the normal pattern
He erred only about the קרבן. He knew the act was forbidden but did not know a קרבן was due.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's statement is needed because שבועת ביטוי is already a חידוש. One might have thought it is also lenient about what counts as שוגג. אביי teaches that even here, a person brings a קרבן only if he did not know the לאו.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'we never find a לאו that brings a קרבן' means a לאו that has no כרת. Normally a חטאת is brought only for sins that carry כרת. That is exactly why שבועת ביטוי is a חידוש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move. An apparently obvious ruling is justified by naming a reasonable mistake (הוה אמינא) that it prevents.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since he is obligated to bring an offering
it is a novel law,
for in the entire Torah
we do not find a prohibition
for which one brings an offering,
and here he does bring one,
so when he erred only regarding the offering
phrases.notes: He knew it was forbidden but did not know a קרבן was due

phrases.english: let him also be liable.
phrases.notes: This is the mistaken conclusion that אביי's statement prevents

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא, הוֹאִיל וְחַיָּיב קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19's challenge that אביי's statement was unnecessary
steps.terutzResolutionType: הוה אמינא justification: the statement prevents a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a קרבן for a לאו without כרת is already a חידוש, perhaps not knowing about the קרבן alone would be enough to make him liable
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי teaches that even for שבועת ביטוי, he brings a קרבן only if he did not know the לאו
